subject: Private deployment: KMS escrow & log access clarifications
messages:
From: Dana Lee <dana.lee@acme-analytics.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Analytics Legal <legal@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions about KMS escrow & log access for on-prem deployment

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for walking us through the private deployment options yesterday. As we move toward procurement, our legal and security teams had a couple of follow-ups so we can confirm the DPA/installation terms:

1) KMS escrow: Acme's security team prefers a customer-controlled key model. They are uncomfortable with any vendor-held escrow except in very tightly-defined circumstances. Can you outline Redwood's position on KMS escrow, specifically:
   - Do you propose any vendor-side escrow or key-recovery mechanism for private (VPC/on-prem) installs?
   - If Redwood requires an escrow to support upgrades/incident recovery, what are the exact triggers and who has access?

2) Log access: For on-prem deployments we expect all customer data plane logs to remain inside our environment. We need clarity on what telemetry Redwood retains/collects from the control plane (metrics, agent heartbeats, stack traces) and whether any PII or request-level content is transmitted off-prem.

3) Subprocessors & cross-border: please send the current subprocessor list and confirm if any downstream subprocessors will process data outside the US for Acme's account.

If useful, I can loop in our compliance lead (Tim Carr from Eversafe) — he has a short list of acceptable escrow controls.

Appreciate a short written summary we can share with legal.

Thanks,
Dana
Dana Lee
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Acme Analytics

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Lee <dana.lee@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Acme Analytics Legal <legal@acme-analytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions about KMS escrow & log access for on-prem deployment

Hi Dana — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary of how Redwood handles these items for Private (VPC/on-prem) customers; I attached an annotated DPA and our latest subprocessors export for your review.

Short summary (TL;DR):
- Customer-controlled keys are supported and the recommended default for on-prem/VPC. Redwood has no unilateral escrow by default.
- We do offer an optional, contractually-scoped escrow arrangement but only under narrow, auditable triggers (court order or joint incident recovery process) and with multi-party approval.
- Data-plane/request-level logs remain in the customer's network for on-prem installs. Control plane telemetry is minimal, pseudonymized where possible, and excludes request payloads.

Details:
1) KMS / Escrow model
   - Default: Customer-managed KMS (customer supplies keys or integrates with their HSM/KMS). Redwood does not hold plaintext customer keys.
   - Optional Escrow: If a customer requests Redwood-managed backup keys to support hands-off upgrades or emergency recovery, the following apply:
     • Escrow keys are encrypted with a separate escrow envelope key held in a third-party neutral HSM (we propose a commercial HSM provider; details in attached doc).
     • Escrow access requires a documented trigger: (a) validated judicial/government order, or (b) mutually-agreed incident recovery request, signed by named customer security contacts and a Redwood security officer.
     • All escrow access events are logged, time-stamped, and subject to quarterly audit checks.
   - Proposed contract language is in proposed_kms_escrow_clause.docx (attached).

2) Logs & telemetry
   - On-prem/VPC data-plane logs (request/response bodies, user prompts, model outputs): never exported by Redwood unless explicitly enabled by the customer.
   - Control-plane telemetry: we collect metrics (CPU/GPU utilization, agent heartbeat, anonymized exception counts). We do not collect request-level content.
   - We can offer a custom telemetry allowlist for Acme that restricts any IPs or hostnames from leaving your VPC.

3) Subprocessors & transfers
   - subprocessors_export_20270424.csv attached lists contractors and cloud partners used for control-plane operations; we highlighted any non-US jurisdictions.
   - For Private deployments, we commit to a subprocessor notification window (30 days) and will not onboard new legal jurisdictions for Acme's account without your written approval.

Next steps:
- I attached an annotated DPA (Redwood_Private_DPA_annotated.pdf) with inline comments for the clauses above.
- If helpful, we can schedule a short call with Redwood Security (Vivek) and our compliance partner (Marissa) + your Tim to agree final escrow triggers and telemetry allowlist.

Let me know which items you want tightened to specific contract language and I can coordinate legal to produce a tracked-change DPA.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Private_DPA_annotated.pdf, subprocessors_export_20270424.csv, proposed_kms_escrow_clause.docx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dana Lee <dana.lee@acme-analytics.com>, Acme Analytics Legal <legal@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions about KMS escrow & log access for on-prem deployment

Thanks all — quick note from legal/security perspective to make the contract defensible and keep risk acceptable for both sides.

Olga, your summary is accurate. A few clarifications I'd like to record in the DPA edits we propose (I'll ask Legal to produce tracked changes):

- Escrow access conditions: we will require a dual-approval model (Redwood security lead + named Acme security contact) for any non-judicial access. Judicial orders are handled per standard legal process but we will notify Acme within 48 hours and provide redaction where permitted.
- Proof-of-accessability testing: if escrow is enabled, Redwood will provide periodic (annual) proof-of-play exercises demonstrating we can retrieve keys from the escrow HSM without exposing keys to Redwood engineers; customer may witness or request a third-party auditor.
- Data minimization clause: add explicit DPA text that control-plane telemetry excludes PII and request payloads; include a binding representation that no request-level content will be stored off-prem without explicit opt-in.
- Subprocessor geo-lock: for Acme's account, lock geography to US-only subprocessors for both support and control-plane processing unless Acme approves in writing.

I'll loop Legal and ask them to prepare the redlines this week. Olga — please share the customer's list of named security contacts and the preferred point of contact for dual-approval.

Onward,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
